Hi :) I don’t know about the other question about finances but about the first question. I’m from Austria so it’s close enough haha. For me the lifestyle is wayyyyy better, but it comes with its costs. 
People are more open minded, outgoing, direct and honest. Unlike in the DACH region where people are more indirect and behind the back. 
I also love how they’re living and celebrating life. 
If you really don’t make a LOT of money, you probably won’t be able to maintain your standard of living you’re used to from Switzerland. And even if you make mid-money, you also won’t. 
I mean since you’ve mentioned you’re from the bank sector, you could end up being very well paid. But if you’re not, be prepared, to pay a lot of money for a moldy apartment (at least in Tel Aviv), spend a fortune on groceries etc. 
I’ve always lived there on a tight budget and it was doable for me, however, I’m faaaaaar from my lifestyle in Austria. I was able to save more monthly in Austria, go on more travels and trips (maybe also due to the sociopolitical situation) and could afford „nice to have things“ like random accessories/furnitures/decoration things. 

The health system is pretty good in Israel I would say. I got doc appointments faster than in Austria. 

Again I don’t know your sector, but I know a lot of Israelis who have lost their job now due to the war. The hi tech sector was in an economical crisis from 2023 on, so I also know a lot of lads who took months or a year to find a job. 

I think it all depends on your qualifications and former positions. I have a friend she was head of anti money laundering and she was even offered to go on a job visa here and double her salary than in Europe. But I mean, that’s a super high position. 

And no one I know ever has converted their degree here.
